headline: Margins narrow while pending Santander sale advances

kpis.label: Return on average tangible common equity

summary_short: Webster Bank posted Q2 2026 diluted EPS of $1.56 (+2.6% y/y) as net interest margin narrowed to 3.26% and non-interest expense rose on Banco Santander transaction costs, while CET1 climbed to 11.71%.
summary_long: Net interest income rose 1.9% y/y as average loans (+8.0%) and deposits (+5.8%) grew, though NIM narrowed to 3.26% from 3.44% on lower rates. Non-interest income climbed 13.3% (BOLI, SecureSave), while non-interest expense rose 11.4%, including $7.6M of Banco Santander transaction costs. Provision for credit losses fell 32.3% on favorable risk migration. Diluted EPS rose to $1.56 as a lower share count offset flat net income. CET1 improved to 11.71% and tangible book value per share rose to $38.81; buybacks remain paused pending the Santander acquisition, expected to close in the second half of 2026.

Webster remains under a definitive agreement to be acquired by Banco Santander (~$12.3B; $48.75 cash + 2.0548 ADSs per share), stockholder-approved and OCC/ECB-cleared, awaiting Federal Reserve approval and expected to close in H2 2026; the Company paused share repurchases and incurred $8.7M of Transaction expenses this quarter as a result.

drivers.explanation: Average asset yields fell 32bps and funding costs fell only 16bps, both due to the lower rate environment and a shift in balance-sheet mix.
Non-interest expense rose 11.4% y/y on higher compensation/incentives (+$24.4M) and $7.6M of Banco Santander transaction expenses, outpacing revenue growth.
Favorable risk-rating migration and lower individually assessed reserves drove the decline, partially offset by higher charge-offs and loan growth.

drivers.metric: Return on average tangible common equity
drivers.explanation: Average tangible common equity grew faster than net income y/y, mechanically compressing the ratio even as absolute ROTCE stayed strong.
A higher effective tax rate (20.6% vs 20.0%) from lower net discrete tax benefits offset growth in pre-tax income.
Net interest income rose 1.9% on higher average loan and deposit balances; non-interest income rose 13.3% on BOLI income, a CVA change, and the SecureSave acquisition.
A 3.6% reduction in weighted-average diluted shares from prior buybacks offset the slight net income decline, lifting EPS.
Capital accreted through retained earnings while the Company paused share repurchases pending the Banco Santander transaction.
Growth in tangible common equity from retained earnings, combined with a smaller share count, lifted TBV per share.
Equity rose on $257M of quarterly net income, partially offset by common and preferred dividends paid.

Webster remains under a definitive agreement to be acquired by Banco Santander (~$12.3B; $48.75 cash + 2.0548 ADSs per share), approved by stockholders and cleared by the OCC and ECB, pending Federal Reserve approval and expected to close in H2 2026.
